note: The purest good-to-great case in the batch — sub-10% body fat, visible abs, plateaued for years, and his own framing is 'I've just been in this zone for so long that I need to get in a good program and get to the next level.' Successful holds squarely: a Meta job plus a company he is founding, self-described as a business guy. Not deconditioned is beyond argument. He fails on the other two. Health is not the neglected area, it is the area he manages most carefully — tennis twice a week, 20-mile rides, rock climbing, lifting, organic and gluten-free eating around an autoimmune condition — so the tension the pitch depends on is absent, and the rep and prospect together concluded 'the value diminishes'. Income fails on willingness rather than capacity: capital is committed to the startup and he said no within seconds, though he also said he would buy with unlimited funds. The notable detail is that the rep recited the ICP definition to him almost verbatim — 'it's people who are already great and they were already good and they want to be great' — while losing him. The stated ICP selects for people who have already solved the problem it sells the solution to.
